Text: Sleek river folk who would rather swim than walk. Otters dig, filter and farm the water from day one, but they are slow on land and work slower once their fur dries out. Their motto: Clean water, warm dens, and a good swim.
The rivers ran dry, and your Otters with them. This is the end.
Congratulations! You mastered the Otters' water-bound ways and used this map's rivers to build the faction's wonder.
The rivers run clean again, and every one of them leads home.
Dry fur: works slower until wet again.
"Why blow it up when you can just dig?"

A pump station that drinks through a tied bundle of reeds. Turns badwater at its intake into clean water without lowering the river; cleans faster the dirtier the water is. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
The reeds don't mind the taste.
A long soak in clean water that washes badwater contamination out of an otter's fur. Uses water.
In through the badwater, out through the rinse.
Builders slowly dig out the block of terrain underneath by paw and leave 1 dirt behind for every block. No explosives, and the digging waits until nobody is standing on the spot.

A cosy otter den built out in the water. Must be placed with at least two tiles in water. Residents' fur dries out more slowly while they sleep. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.

A two-storey otter den out in the water for six. Must be placed with at least three tiles in water. Residents' fur dries out more slowly while they sleep. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
Grows with its feet in the water and its head in the sun.
Big leaves above, starchy roots below.

A fisher drops a line into the water below and brings up fish. Needs water under the line; the more badwater in it, the fewer fish bite, and none at all in half-badwater. Takes no water from the river. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
Patience, a long rod, and a longer lunch.

A log-framed swimming hole set into the river, with a deck, a diving board and a bench. Fun for everyone; otters' fur gets a good soak. Needs water inside the frame. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
Last one in is a dry beaver.

Drills deep and brings up clean water out of nowhere: no aquifer needed, and it keeps flowing through droughts (at half speed) and badtides. Needs an operator and 750 hp of power. Build it with its back to lower ground or open water: the water spills out over the edge behind it until it is nearly level with the well. Or plug Water Tubes into its side walls or back to send the water to Tube Outlets elsewhere. Every so often the pump breaks down and the operator has to spend a few hours repairing it before water flows again.
Deep down, the river never ends.
Broken down: the operator is repairing it. No water until it's fixed.
The water has nowhere to go. Build the well with its back to lower ground or water, or connect Water Tubes to a Tube Outlet that pours over an edge.
Well water has nowhere to go

Carries water from an Artesian Well to Tube Outlets. Plug a line into the well's left wall, right wall or back; when outlets are connected, all of the well's water goes to them, shared evenly, instead of spilling out behind the well.
The open end of a water tube line. Connect a tube to its back and build it with its spout over lower ground or water; it pours until the water below is nearly up to the spout.
Where the river comes back out.
Smokes fish over a slow log fire. One fish makes three smoked fish, the otters' favourite food.

A slide tower on the bank with a chute that drops into the river. Fun for everyone and a thorough soaking for otters. Needs water at the bottom of the chute. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.

A mud-and-log ramp down the bank. Build it on the riverbed against the bank, facing the bank, and otters can slip into the river and swim along the bottom instead of walking around. Works like stairs for everyone.

A length of Water Tube with a hand wheel. Pause it to close it: no water gets past it, so outlets beyond it go dry and the rest of the line shares the well's water. If every outlet on a well's line is closed off, the well stops pumping instead of spilling behind it. Paused Tube Outlets get no water either.
Every Tube Outlet on this well's line is paused or closed off by a Tube Valve, so the water stays in the well.

A staked net over the riverbed where a gatherer raises clams. Build it with its deck on the bank and its bed over water one block down. Needs at least half a block of water over the bed, and clean water: the more badwater, the fewer clams, and none at all at 20% badwater. Takes no water from the river. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
Happy as a clam, as long as the water's clean.
No clams: the bed needs at least half a block of clean water (under 20% badwater) over it.

A log boom across the current that catches driftwood and lands it as logs. Build it with its deck on the bank and the boom over water one block down. Only works in moving water, faster the stronger the current (full speed from a current of 1). Needs no trees and takes no water. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
Somebody upstream is very bad at keeping track of their logs.
Nothing drifts in: the boom needs moving water (a current of at least 0.05) at least a third of a block deep.
A low sun deck with reed mats and a warm flat stone. Otters sprawl here to dry off and doze in the sun. Waterproof: keeps working when the water rises over its door.
Wet fur, warm stone, no plans.

The Otters' wonder: a great log fountain that lifts the river into a bowl high above the town and pours it back in four streams, with a holt on top. Once finished and stocked with extract and smoked fish it can be activated, filling every otter nearby with awe and keeping their fur wet.
Every river starts somewhere. This one starts here.
